title: Build Grafana dashboards + alerting for Dedicated throughput SLO (by tier)
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
Context
- Dedicated throughput tiers are being productized and we need a consistent, enforceable SLO. This issue covers the operator + customer-facing observability layer: Grafana dashboards and alerting rules.
- Must align to the measurement standard + tier semantics being defined in the throughput PRD/ADRs.

Goal
- Provide a single Grafana "Dedicated Throughput" dashboard suite and production-grade alert rules that:
  1) show SLI vs objective per deployment and tier
  2) surface leading indicators (throttling, queue depth, saturation)
  3) page the right oncall with good hygiene (low noise, clear actionability)

Non-goals
- No redesign of Console UX beyond linking to/exporting the same metrics.
- Not re-implementing metric emission in runtime/gateway (see ENG-2194). We may add minor recording rules if needed.

Requirements (dashboards)
Create Grafana dashboards in a dedicated folder: "Dedicated / Throughput SLO".

1) Overview (by deployment)
- Panels:
  - Throughput SLI (effective output tokens/sec) vs tier objective (overlay)
  - SLO compliance (rolling window) + error budget remaining (by tier)
  - Throttling rate (requests throttled / total) and top throttling reasons
  - Queue depth + queue time (p50/p95) for prefill + decode
  - Request concurrency, active streams, and admission control state (normal/burst/overload)
- Filters/templating:
  - deployment_id (required)
  - tier, region, model (optional)
- Notes:
  - Ensure the dashboard still renders when deployment_id cardinality is high (use variables + top-N tables rather than plotting all deployments).

2) Fleet/Tier view (by tier/region)
- Panels:
  - Aggregate throughput SLI distribution by tier (p50/p95 across deployments)
  - % time in burst mode / overload mode
  - Saturation indicators: GPU util, KV cache eviction rate (if available), batcher saturation
  - "No data" and label health (deployments missing required labels)

3) Customer export view (lightweight)
- Intended for CS/Support to screenshot/export quickly.
- Panels:
  - Throughput SLI vs objective
  - Throttling rate
  - Queue depth
  - Incidents/annotations (maintenance windows + known incidents)

Requirements (alerts)
Implement alert rules + routing in the observability-pack:

A) SLO burn / SLO at risk
- Multi-window, multi-burn style alerts (fast burn + slow burn).
- Pages Dedicated oncall (SRE) only when action is required.
- Alerts must group/dedupe by deployment_id + region (avoid paging a separate alert per model unless model is the primary dimension of impact).
- Include:
  - tier
  - deployment_id
  - region
  - current SLI, objective, and estimated time-to-exhaust error budget
  - link to dashboard + runbook

B) Leading indicators (ticket/Slack, not page unless severe)
- sustained high throttling (>X% over Y minutes)
- sustained queue depth / queue time above threshold
- sustained overload mode (e.g., overload_state=1) beyond expected burst window
- missing metrics/no data for a deployment in a tiered Dedicated pool (this should page during rollout, then become a ticket once stable)

C) Paging hygiene / operational guardrails
- Severity levels:
  - SEV2 page: SLO burn fast-burn (customer-visible breach likely within hours)
  - SEV3 page: SLO burn slow-burn (risk) ONLY for Premium tier during beta; otherwise Slack
  - Ticket: leading indicators unless paired with SLO burn
- Add alert annotations:
  - runbook URL
  - owner team (SRE/Infra/Runtime)
  - "expected during maintenance" note with link to maintenance schedule policy
- Silence rules:
  - planned maintenance windows and known fleet events (coordinate with Infra)
- Noise checks before paging:
  - run 7-day backtest in staging + 3-5 pilot Dedicated deployments
  - ensure alert fires < 1/day per deployment in normal operation

Data sources / assumptions
- Depends on throughput SLI metrics and standardized labels from ENG-2194.
- Expected labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, customer_id (customer_id optional for internal-only panels).
- SLI definition and exclusions per Dedicated throughput SLO definition Confluence doc.

Implementation plan
1) Draft dashboards based on spec; validate panel queries against metrics taxonomy.
2) Add recording rules as needed (e.g., rate over standardized window, burn-rate helpers).
3) Implement alert rules and route in Alertmanager (Dedicated oncall).
4) Run pilot with 3–5 Dedicated deployments (include at least one Premium candidate + one Standard).
5) Enable paging for Premium first; then Performance; then Standard (or keep Standard as Slack-only depending on policy).

Acceptance criteria
- Grafana dashboards merged and visible in prod Grafana:
  - Dedicated / Throughput SLO / Overview
  - Dedicated / Throughput SLO / Fleet + Tier
  - Dedicated / Throughput SLO / Customer Export
- Alert rules merged and deployed:
  - SLO burn (fast + slow burn) for throughput SLI
  - Leading indicators (throttling, queue depth/queue time, overload state)
  - No-data/label-health alert during rollout (can be downgraded after rollout)
- Every alert has:
  - clear summary + next action
  - dashboard link
  - runbook link
  - correct routing + dedupe behavior
- Paging hygiene sign-off from Aisha Bello + Rafael Mendes:
  - backtest evidence linked in ticket
  - initial thresholds documented
  - rollback plan (disable paging via feature flag / alert routing toggle)

Open questions
- Final tier objectives and which tiers page by default (depends on Product + SRE policy).
- Whether to include prefill/decode breakdown in customer export view or keep internal-only.

Notes
- Coordinate with ENG-2206 (admission control hooks) so dashboard accurately reflects expected throttling vs true degradation.
- If we can annotate dashboards with overload/maintenance events automatically, we should (even if v1 is manual annotations).
comments:
2025-02-03 — Sergio Costa:
Drafted initial dashboard panels based on the Confluence spec. Main open question is grouping: plotting time series for all deployments explodes. Plan is variable-driven overview (single deployment at a time) + top-N tables for fleet view. I’ll share screenshots once queries are stable.

Action: need final metric names/labels from ENG-2194 to avoid rework.

2025-02-07 — Logan Wright:
Metrics taxonomy update: we’re standardizing on deployment_id, tier, region, model. customer_id may be absent for some internal perf-canary deployments. Recommend dashboards avoid customer_id as a required filter.

Also note: effective_toks_per_sec should be computed from output tokens, excluding throttled requests (throttled should be tracked separately).

2025-02-11 — Aisha Bello:
Alerting guidance:
- Use multi-window burn rates. Page only for fast-burn. Slow-burn should be Slack during beta except Premium.
- No-data should page during first 2 weeks of rollout, then downgrade to ticket.
- Make sure we have explicit silences for planned maintenance and a clear "expected throttling" panel so Support doesn’t treat throttling as an incident by default.

2025-02-18 — Sergio Costa:
Implemented alert rules in observability-pack branch with routing to Dedicated oncall. Added runbook links and dashboard deep links (deployment_id pre-selected).

Backtest (staging + 4 pilot deployments) shows:
- fast-burn fired 2x during induced overload (expected)
- slow-burn fired once during a perf-canary regression (good signal)
- throttling alert was noisy; raising threshold + requiring sustained window.

Next: request SRE signoff + merge.

2025-03-04 — Rafael Mendes:
Reviewed alert thresholds + grouping. Request changes before paging enablement:
1) group_by should include region; exclude model.
2) add annotation with "admission_control_state" when available (to distinguish overload vs regression).
3) create a single "label health" alert for missing tier/region labels (ticket-only).

Once addressed, OK to enable paging for Premium pilot.

2025-03-06 — Sergio Costa:
Addressed Rafael’s feedback. Grouping updated; model removed from dedupe. Added label-health alert (ticket-only) and updated throttling rule to require both high throttling + elevated queue time.

Ready for final review/merge.
